task.description: Adjudicate ELIXIR-DEV's BLOCKER: implementing the approved design's literal `max_concurrency: 8` for the 6 Admission-gated sweeps breaks 4 REQ-218 tests when `Admission.global_cap` is configured below 8 (e.g. pool_size:3/reserved_headroom:2 -> global_cap:1). Decide between (a) design gap -- derive max_concurrency live from a new `Admission.global_cap/1` accessor -- or (b) test gap -- REQ-218's 4 tests encode a stricter invariant than the design promises and should be relaxed.

result.summary:
Confirmed ELIXIR-DEV's diagnosis by direct inspection (not taken on faith): read the actual diff (git diff main...feature/WF03-ISS0421-20260904 -- lib/letflow/admission.ex lib/letflow/scheduler.ex lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex) and the actual call site -- `@admission_gated_max_concurrency 8` (poller.ex, module attribute) is passed as `max_concurrency:` to `Task.async_stream/3` at all 6 Admission-gated sweep call sites via the new `run_sweep/4` helper, unconditionally, regardless of the live `Admission.global_cap` of whatever server instance is actually running. Also read test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs in full: REQ-218 AC1, AC2, and the AC3 per-schema clause all call `AdmissionTestHelpers.restart_admission!(pool_size: 3, reserved_headroom: 2)` (global_cap == 1) specifically to get deterministic, race-free admission behavior, and AC2's own code comment states the invariant plainly: 'A single, sequential caller (Poller) never holds more than one admission unit at a time... so with global_cap == 1 and NO concurrent contender, Poller's own acquire/release round trips never collide with each other -- every attempt succeeds.' That invariant is real code in this repo today (a `describe` block with a load-bearing comment explaining WHY the test is deterministic), not an incidental assumption -- it was true before this change and the new `Task.async_stream(max_concurrency: 8)` call structurally breaks it whenever live `global_cap < 8` by making Poller its own concurrent contender for its own admission slot.

DECISION: (a) -- this is a genuine design gap, not a test gap. Reasoning:

1. The design's own §3a safety argument ('peak DBConnection checkouts attributable to these six sweeps is bounded by Admission.global_cap = 8') is technically still true as a peak-safety claim -- a rejected task never reaches a Repo call, `try_acquire/2` is a pure in-memory GenServer.call gate, so no DBConnection checkout, let alone pool thrashing, occurs for a task that loses the race. I explicitly do not adopt the 'DB connection pool thrashing' framing from the handoff prompt as a real cost here -- it isn't one, by the code's own structure.
2. BUT the design's §3a arithmetic silently assumes `max_concurrency (8) <= live global_cap` always holds, treating 8 as a universal constant rather than as 'the value that happens to equal `Admission.global_cap` at today's default config.' That assumption is false whenever `Admission.global_cap != 8` -- which is not a hypothetical: `global_cap = pool_size - reserved_headroom`, `pool_size` is explicitly documented in this same design doc (§1) as an operator-configurable `POOL_SIZE` env var read at `config/runtime.exs:113`, defaulting to 10 but not fixed at 10. A smaller deployment tier, or any operator lowering `POOL_SIZE`, silently reintroduces self-collision in production, not just in tests -- the tests merely make an already-real production hazard deterministic and visible, they are not inventing an artificial scenario. This is the exact 'literal number that happens to match another instance's derived value today, with nothing tying the two together' class of hazard CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's rework-1 FAIL already caught once in this same design for `reserved_headroom` (`handoffs/WF03-ISS0421-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator.json`, finding 2) -- the design's own §3b already rejects a hardcoded-literal-plus-comment approach for that reason ('a hardcoded Poller-side 2... nothing tied [it] to [Admission's real value], so a future change to one without the other would silently push the combined worst-case peak past pool_size with no backstop to catch it'). §3a makes the identical mistake the design's own §3b explicitly reasoned its way out of, one section earlier in the same document, for the sibling sweep. That is an internal inconsistency in the design, not merely an incomplete one.
3. Consequence beyond the 4 failing tests: at any live `global_cap < 8`, Poller's own concurrently-dispatched tasks for ONE sweep now race each other for the same slot(s), and `Task.async_stream` does not retry a rejected item -- it only advances to the next schema in the list as a slot frees. This means schemas late in `tenant_schemas/0`'s returned order are systematically disadvantaged relative to early ones under sustained tight-cap conditions (a real fairness/starvation risk, not just 'try again next tick' -- a schema that is always last in a stable-ordered list could be skipped every tick if earlier schemas keep winning the race), which is a materially worse property than today's fully-serial 'every schema gets a real, uncontested attempt against a shrunk cap.' This is a new problem introduced by the fix, in a config region the fix's own author (this same design doc) explicitly built the reserved_headroom half of this exact fix to avoid.
4. I therefore reject option (b) (relaxing the 4 REQ-218 tests): the stricter property they encode ('Poller never becomes its own contender when it is the only caller and cap >= 1') is not test over-specification -- it is a real, previously-guaranteed platform property, worth preserving as written, and cheaply preservable by mirroring a pattern this same design has already adopted once (the `reserved_headroom/1` live accessor). Weakening the tests to match a needlessly fragile implementation would just relocate the operator-configurable-POOL_SIZE hazard from 'caught by 4 failing tests today' to 'silently live in production until someone runs with a smaller pool,' which is strictly worse, not neutral.

ROUTING: back to CODE-DESIGNER for a third design rework (a new round at this Step 4 gate, not a continuation of the exhausted Step 2b rework counter -- that counter belongs to a different gate and is not consumed by this decision). Required change, precisely scoped:

- Add `Letflow.Admission.global_cap/1` (default `server \\ __MODULE__`), delegating via `GenServer.call/2` to a new `handle_call(:global_cap, _from, state)` clause replying `state.global_cap` unchanged -- byte-for-byte the same idiom already used for `reserved_headroom/1` (admission.ex, this same branch), since `global_cap` is ALREADY a state field (`state.global_cap`, admission.ex:245) -- no new state-shape change is needed here, unlike `reserved_headroom` which required one. This is strictly smaller in scope than the rework that added `reserved_headroom/1`.
- `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex`'s 6 Admission-gated sweeps: replace `@admission_gated_max_concurrency 8` (module attribute, literal) with a live call to `Letflow.Admission.global_cap/0`, read fresh inside `run_sweep/4` (or each call site) every invocation -- never cached or hoisted -- mirroring exactly the convention already established for `maybe_refresh_active_instances/1`'s `Admission.reserved_headroom()` call in this same diff. This makes both halves of the design (§3a and §3b) use the identical 'read the real accessor live' pattern instead of one doing so and the other hardcoding a number that merely matches it today.
- Re-verify §3c's algebraic sanity check (`max(global_cap, reserved_headroom)` peak) still holds with a live-derived `global_cap` in §3a -- it does, since the identity was already stated in terms of `global_cap`/`reserved_headroom` as values, not as the literal 8/2; only the SOURCE of the number in code changes, not the arithmetic.
- This closes the underlying test failures as a side effect, not a special case: at test config `pool_size: 3, reserved_headroom: 2` -> `global_cap: 1`, a live-derived `max_concurrency` becomes 1, restoring exactly the pre-fix 'Poller never holds more than one admission unit concurrently' property REQ-218 AC1/AC2/AC3-per-schema/AC5 depend on, with NO changes needed to poller_test.exs.

SCOPE NOTE (creep check, per REVIEWER's own §4 mandate): this rework is NOT scope creep -- it does not introduce new abstractions, only extends a pattern (`live GenServer-state accessor` for a `Task.async_stream` bound) this same design already introduced once, to the one place it should have been applied but wasn't. Idiom/supervision/type-safety findings on the rest of the diff, for when this rework lands, are recorded below so ELIXIR-DEV/CODE-DESIGNER do not need to re-derive them.

IDIOM REVIEW OF THE REST OF THE DIFF (independent of the BLOCKER above -- these are not gating, informational for the next round):
- Supervision: unaffected. No new process is added outside the existing Poller `GenServer`; `Task.async_stream/3`'s unnamed/unsupervised task pool is bounded, fully consumed (`Enum.each`/`Enum.reduce` over the whole stream), and time-bounded (`on_timeout: :kill_task`) at every call site -- no orphaned or unsupervised long-lived process is created. This is an acceptable, idiomatic use of the *unnamed* Task pool specifically because (per design §8) no task needs to outlive the calling `handle_info/2` invocation or be independently observable/killable -- correctly distinguished from `Letflow.SandboxPool`'s `Task.Supervisor` use, which exists for a materially different lifetime requirement. No `Letflow.InstanceSupervisor`-per-instance concern applies here at all -- this change is scheduler/admission internals, not instance lifecycle.
- Idiomatic vs. crutch: `run_sweep/4`'s helper correctly centralizes the `Task.async_stream` options and exit-logging instead of duplicating them at 6 call sites -- good factoring, not premature abstraction (it is used exactly 6 times, all with the same shape, today).
- Type-safety: no new class of invalid state is introduced by this diff (no new struct/schema, no new transition). Not filing a type-safety issue for this diff.
- Genuinely new, already-flagged coverage gap (not mine to fix, noted so it isn't lost): ELIXIR-DEV's own mutation-testing note in step-03's handoff found no existing test asserts `maybe_refresh_active_instances/1`'s `max_concurrency` actually tracks a NON-default `Admission.reserved_headroom()`. That gap is real and separate from this BLOCKER; route it to TEST-DESIGNER once this rework's own new `global_cap/1` accessor exists too, so both live-derivation call sites (`reserved_headroom/1` for the unwrapped sweep, `global_cap/1` for the 6 gated sweeps) get an equivalent non-default-value regression test in the same pass, rather than filing two separate follow-ups.

Do not route to TEST-DESIGNER yet. This must return through CODE-DESIGNER (design change) -> CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (4th pass) -> ELIXIR-DEV (small, mechanical implementation: one new accessor + swap one literal for a live call) -> REVIEWER (re-check) before TEST-DESIGNER touches anything. No changes to test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs are authorized by this verdict.

gate_history.notes: Design gap confirmed: iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md §3a hardcodes max_concurrency: 8 for the 6 Admission-gated sweeps instead of deriving it live from Admission.global_cap, unlike §3b's own (correct) live-derivation of reserved_headroom for the 7th sweep. Routed to CODE-DESIGNER for a 3rd design rework adding Letflow.Admission.global_cap/1 and using it live in poller.ex; REQ-218's 4 currently-failing tests are correct as written and must NOT be weakened.
